summary: @workoscalifant/sudoku-term executes opaque Go binary at install time that contradicts documented C source
details: The postinstall script scripts/postinstall.js invokes execFileSync on prebuilt/linux-x64/sudoku-hint with a --selftest argument on every npm install on Linux x64. The shipped binary is 33,976,468 bytes and contains Go runtime metadata (runtime., reflect., GODEBUG, godebugs.Info) and /proc/self/cgroup and /proc/self/mountinfo self-probe strings. The package's declared source is native/hint.c, a small dependency-free C solver, and the README describes the Linux artifact as a 26 KB static-musl ELF that reads no files and opens no sockets. The shipped build.sh cannot produce a 34 MB Go binary from a ~200-line C file. The macOS sibling artifact matches the declared C source; the Linux artifact does not. Installer harm: whatever code the Go binary contains executes on every Linux x64 machine that runs npm install for this package, and the shipped source is structured so that the binary's behavior cannot be reconstructed or audited from the tarball.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
